title: Rahzaan: AI Career Guidance Platform
layer2: Deployed agentic counselling platform for Pakistani secondary school students. The hard part is reasoning truthfully about eligibility: multiple exam boards with different percentage conversions, five streams, regulatory gating by several councils with distinct minima (PEC at 60% for BE, HEC at 50% for BS, 45% elsewhere) and merit rules that are often unpublished. Primary architect and director.
layer1: Built the platform's evaluation harness: 60 per-turn traces, 19 behavioural probes, and a 46-file behavioural test suite of 592 automated tests.
detail: Deployed agentic counselling platform for Pakistani secondary school students.
bullets: Built the platform's evaluation harness: five named personas and a ten-scenario curriculum matrix producing 60 per-turn traces, 19 behavioural probes using paired before-and-after measurement and single-criterion isolation to attribute cause, a separated run-and-analyse pipeline, and a 46-file behavioural test suite of 592 automated tests catching regressions before users hit them.

Refuted my own diagnosis of why the system over-asserted. I assumed thin data caused it; measuring across five data-completeness levels showed the opposite, the thinnest persona was the most honest, declining outright rather than fabricating. The real trigger was internal signal divergence, the model inventing an affective bridge to reconcile conflicting academic and psychometric inputs, so the scarcity guard I had planned would have fixed nothing. Redirected the fix to the divergence path, then added a deterministic post-generation gate as backstop after establishing that negative directives carry a reliability ceiling.

Architected a 24-node LangGraph pipeline: fan-out across 9 concurrent nodes, fan-in through a central dispatcher, then two further stages, with 52 typed state fields and concurrent-write reducers. Cut first-response latency from 20 to 25 seconds down to 3.7 seconds. Per-node model routing lets any node's LLM be swapped through environment config alone, with LangSmith tracing for per-turn execution, node latency, and token usage.

Built a production FastAPI backend: 22 REST endpoints, LangGraph checkpoint persistence to PostgreSQL, SSE streaming with a parallel keepalive task that defeats the host's 30-second proxy timeout, JWT authentication with bcrypt, rate limiting, 11 Alembic migrations against live data, a deterministic refresh endpoint that regenerates recommendations with zero LLM calls, and a profile summary generator running six parallel LLM calls plus synthesis off the event loop. Automated a 15-day job-market pipeline mapping 14,595 job titles to canonical career fields via Gemini.

Engineered two model-independent LLM guardrails: a 9-criterion reflection gate that applies surgical corrections before any response streams, including a check that blocks unfounded emotional or clinical claims about a user, and deterministic context stripping, built after finding the model ignores "do not include" instructions but cannot discuss data it never receives. Verified across two model versions, alongside three callable tool interfaces and PII handling kept as concerns separate from the agents themselves.

Shipped a 29-route Flutter frontend: onboarding, six assessment flows, O/A Level grade conversion, live streaming chat, recommendation dashboard, and a profile hub. Riverpod state management and cold-start timeout handling. Web build deployed on Vercel (live), with a contract test on the frontend asserting the same merit-tier contract the backend enforces.

Designed the recommendation engine: a 265-item session drawn from item banks of 1,409, sized so a student who reassesses is not asked the same questions twice, across seven construct-grounded psychometric instruments including an original one derived from work-adjustment theory, with MBTI rejected on published reliability evidence. Scored by a multi-dimensional model blending interest-profile geometry, measured capability, and deterministic tier validation with no LLM call. Fully bilingual: every instrument and the entire session exist in English and Roman Urdu, and the conversation follows whichever the student uses, including mixed script within a sentence.

Ran the build through a two-tier development harness of my own design, now my default method for any system of size: an architecture conversation producing versioned specifications, an implementer working from them under a written rules file across five role-scoped instruction sets, and LangSmith traces pulled back through a fetch skill to close the loop. Recorded across 334 session records in four months with the model and reasoning tier attributed per session, 53 audit documents over six whole-system audit phases, and a status register tagging every claim live-verified or believed so that doubt stays pointed at the unverified set.

Coordinated two contributors through written setup guides, versioned interface contracts and 17 dated change notices, against a governance document versioned to v2.27 carrying 80+ locked decisions, with rehearsal runs before every destructive data operation and a documentation toolchain generating both the architecture view and the dissertation itself from code.

title: Applied LLM Workflow Research
layer2: Behavioural study of Gemini 2.5 Pro identifying reproducible failure modes in production LLM workflows.
layer1: Identified and named three failure modes: Optimal Answer Trap, Final Synthesis Bias, and Conversational Gravity, each reproduced through documented prompt sequences.
detail: Behavioural study of Gemini 2.5 Pro identifying reproducible failure modes in production LLM workflows.
bullets: Identified and named three failure modes: Optimal Answer Trap (the model locks onto its first acceptable answer and resists valid redirection), Final Synthesis Bias (output collapses toward a synthesised endpoint regardless of instruction), and Conversational Gravity (accumulated context progressively narrows model behaviour), each reproduced through documented prompt sequences.

Ran controlled experiments across temperature, top-p, and top-k sampling; 1M-token context stress tests; adversarial red-teaming with hallucination injection; and context-ordering trials showing a ~30% retrieval error rate when context follows rather than precedes the instruction.

Shipped a 5-stage prompting protocol combining intent decomposition, strict output schemas, and adversarial self-critique, deployed as an interactive Streamlit application with a failure-mode comparison view and a prompt template playground (live).

title: ChatGPT Deep Research Provenance Case Study
layer2: Black-box investigation of a production AI research agent: ChatGPT Deep Research runs that displayed "Research completed" with 0 searches and 0 citations while still producing substantive, source-specific reports. I conceived and ran the investigation, made every evidence, claim and publication decision, refined the design with ChatGPT as my architecture chat and delegated the supporting code and documentation to Codex for speed.
layer1: Reduced research briefs of 974 to 1,757 words to a 55-word canary that tells the system to report failure if it retrieves no sources.
detail: Black-box investigation of a production AI research agent.
bullets: Preserved a baseline of 9 earlier runs that had displayed 2,835 searches and 477 citations, then reduced research briefs of 974 to 1,757 words to a 55-word canary that tells the system to report failure if it retrieves no sources. The canary still completed at 0/0 on four accounts (one Plus, three Free) across desktop web, the iOS app and macOS Safari, and again three days later; all 14 runs since the baseline displayed zero of both.

Instrumented a fresh reproduction with browser diagnostics and captured the client's own warning that the report "contains citation markers but no content references". Checked the run's policy figures against the central banks' official sites: it reported a Bank of Canada rate change published hours earlier, so a zero counter is no evidence that current information failed to reach it. Kept every conclusion at the level of the evidence: no root-cause or retrieval claim, and earlier public reports credited.

Found a separate failure: two completed reports silently covered 1 of 3 and 1 of 4 requested programmes, which is why I treat completion, provenance and scope coverage as separate acceptance criteria for research agents. Published a privacy-bounded case study from a fresh repository, every evidence file checked by SHA-256 in GitHub Actions against an exact manifest, and gave OpenAI Support the sanitized network capture it requested.
Retired my own natural-language checker after reviews found it passing cases that were not clean, and replaced it with deterministic checks on explicit inputs, kept out of the public claim.

title: Job Aggregator: Automated Job Discovery Pipeline
status: In development, and running in production since 17 Sep 2026.
layer2: Unattended pipeline that reads employer job boards on a schedule and shows only eligible postings for review, at no recurring cost. Architect and director: I design the system and its algorithms, make the trade-offs and the decisions, and delegate implementation to Claude Code for speed, under specifications I approve and a development method I designed.
layer1: Cut job discovery from a by-hand baseline I estimated at three to six days to a measured median of 5.4 hours after publication.
detail: In development, and running in production since 17 Sep 2026. Unattended pipeline that reads employer job boards on a schedule and shows only eligible postings for review, at no recurring cost.
bullets: Cut job discovery from a by-hand baseline I estimated at three to six days to a measured median of 5.4 hours after publication, 90th percentile 10.5 hours over 114 postings, against targets of 24 and 72. The pipeline runs on GitHub Actions and Python (standard library plus requests), reading eleven employer ATS boards twice a day and one aggregator daily.

30 production runs over 13.6 days with zero retries and zero failed requests, a median of 36 requests per run against a budget of 500, and 34,557 postings fetched. Retry with backoff, a circuit breaker and three exit codes (done, failed, stopped and resumable) mean a missed run costs latency, never data.

Every posting is admitted or dropped by a named deterministic rule, with no model and no scoring, and every drop is logged. In one run of 1,283 postings, 36 were kept: 922 dropped on title against 79 terms in four role families, 258 on location, 56 on seniority and 11 on age. The location rule dropped exactly the 74 of 91 saved postings its decision record had predicted nine days before it was built. Duplicates are grouped: 824 postings became 527 display rows, and one role posted 134 times, once per city, became one.

Git branches serve as the database, in three layers: a permanent append-only raw layer, a filtered layer, and an Airtable display that is never authoritative. Privacy is enforced in code rather than by care: employer description text and aggregator data never reach the public repository, and every posting is saved in full to a private store, marked saved only after it is read back and matched by content hash. A daily contract check fingerprints each API's field shapes, telling a board that changed its API apart from one with no new jobs.

Ran the build through a four-role AI-native development method of my own design. I bring the blueprint, the architecture and the engineering trade-offs, and set the standards every role works to; an architecture chat refines the design with me into decisions; Claude Code implements to briefs I approve; a fresh read-only reviewer audits cold; and every brief and audit comes back to me to decide. Six independent audits, 55 decision records, 23 session logs and 122 commits on main between 1 Sep and 2 Oct 2026 UTC.

Audited it by using it and caught what the coding agents missed: an age rule built so admitted rows could vanish before I had seen them, rebuilt the same day; and an aggregator endpoint rejected on a test of the wrong parameter, whose re-measurement, prompted by my question, took the feed from 93% irrelevant to every relevant posting, 420 of 420 stored. I approved a title-normalisation change only on a before-and-after comparison of every verdict, and of 1,458 titles exactly one changed, the one intended. I judged that postings reappearing under years-old dates were harvesting CVs, and the measurement afterwards found that 60 of the 83 Greenhouse postings already a week old at first sight were one role, reposted city by city since 2024. When an audit found a deletion path that would have erased my record of roles applied to, I set aside the proposed fix and designed my own.

Covered by 754 tests and 410 recorded mutations that deliberately break the code to prove the tests notice, with 10,381 lines of tests against 6,636 lines of source; the suite fails if a code change leaves any recorded mutation unable to run, and architectural rules are guarded by fitness functions in the ordinary suite. A production save failure on 27 Sep 2026 was found in the morning run log, reproduced, fixed and pushed before the next run, with the postings it missed recovered by the next walk.

title: Portfolio Gallery: Portfolio Site Template and Design Gallery
layer2: A public, MIT-licensed template anyone can copy to publish a one-page portfolio site on GitHub Pages without installing anything: they write their content once, pick one of 17 designs, 10 of them made for professions, and every claim on the site is checked against their own CV; a copy clears the project's own files out of itself on its first run. I started it and maintain it on my own account: I design the system, set its standards, make the decisions and delegate implementation to Claude Code for speed.
layer1: Cut a check of every page from 75.4 minutes on one runner to about 5 by sharing it across parallel jobs.
detail: A public, MIT-licensed template anyone can copy to publish a one-page portfolio site on GitHub Pages without installing anything.
bullets: Designed it to take strangers' pull requests safely: designs are CSS only; a Content Security Policy in every page refuses requests to other sites; a scope check runs from the default branch, so a pull request cannot change how it is checked; contributors' screenshots are redrawn and never served as uploaded, and their sites are fetched but never rendered; every workflow action is pinned to a full commit SHA, the Python dependencies to the SHA-256 of every file PyPI serves, and npm runs with install scripts disabled.

Runs accessibility (axe-core) and speed (Lighthouse) checks in GitHub Actions on every pull request. Cut a check of every page from 75.4 minutes on one runner to about 5 by sharing it across parallel jobs, and set the rule that a pull request is checked only on the pages it alters, with every page rechecked each Monday. The required check cannot pass by being skipped: a verdict job fails unless every part passed or was skipped by plan, proven on a failed, a timed-out and a wrongly skipped part.

Proved every check able to fail: 178 file defeat cases and 24 browser cases, each set with planted controls that must pass. Speed is judged so a noisy shared runner is not mistaken for a slow page: blocking time over its goal is reported, and fails only above 600 ms.

Followed my own setup as a stranger would and turned each friction into a fix a check now guards: resizing a screenshot in Paint became any snip; a copy's first deploy, which failed red while GitHub Pages was off, now ends with a notice saying how to turn it on; the screenshot overlay gained a close button; and when I judged the designs too alike, they became designs per profession, each shown with its own invented sample person and held to a measured distinctness bar of 60 to 75 percent on box placement rather than judged by eye.

Documented it for strangers and their AI tools: a README that routes each visitor to what they came to do and carries a self-contained prompt for their own AI assistant, checked against the repository by a tool so it cannot drift; an AGENTS.md for coding agents; and versions of both that every copy receives.

Run as maintainer: a ruleset requiring a pull request and passing checks for every change to main, CODEOWNERS review, issue forms, a Code of Conduct and private vulnerability reporting. Likes are counted from GitHub Discussions through its GraphQL API, counting only the workflow's posts and mine. 21 decision records, each assumption carrying its basis; three found resting on memory were sourced or measured within the day, one by my own test of how GitHub counts reactions.

title: Portfolio Site
layer2: My one-page portfolio, carrying the evidence a one-page CV cannot hold. I architected it, found the six reference sites its look comes from, prototyped it in Claude Design and delegated implementation to Claude Code for speed.
layer1: Every claim on the page traces to my master CV, checked by a tool in both directions before any content change.
detail: My one-page portfolio, carrying the evidence a one-page CV cannot hold.
bullets: Every claim on the page traces to my master CV, checked by a tool in both directions before any content change. A small Python generator builds one page with every word in the first response, readable without scripts, and refuses content with a missing source or proof link, projects out of rank order, or shortened text that is not a cut of its source. Seven repository gates, run by git hooks, refuse a commit that adds a cookie, tracking, a third-party request or anything private.

Designed its timeline: a vertical spine with lanes either side, newest work at the top so a reader meets the latest first, and on a phone one spine carrying every lane, chosen after viewing both prototype versions on my phone.

Tested it with a screen reader: my NVDA run found words read as one, such as "Dec 20255-Day", which every automated check had passed; I had them fixed with hidden spaces and confirmed the fix by ear the same day. axe-core found 0 violations in 12 combinations of width, theme and panel state, in Chrome and in Edge, and keyboard checks passed 60 of 60.

Measures performance so a slow machine is not mistaken for a slow page: each Lighthouse set runs the page, the page before the change and a control with a deliberate 600 ms script that must fail, five runs each, interleaved. Live median of 1.7 s largest paint against a 2.5 s goal (Oct 2026). Had the reading-layers proposal audited before it was recorded rather than accepted as proposed; the audit changed four things. 13 decision records, each assumption carrying its basis.

title: Autonomous Research Concierge
layer2: Multi-agent research pipeline, containerised and deployed on Railway.
layer1: Engineered a sequential-parallel-loop agent architecture: three live-search agents fan out concurrently, and a draft-critique-validate loop exits on an explicit escalation signal rather than a timeout.
detail: Multi-agent research pipeline, containerised and deployed on Railway.
bullets: Engineered a sequential-parallel-loop agent architecture: an intent synthesiser compacts chat history into a research directive, three live-search agents fan out concurrently, and a draft-critique-validate loop exits on an explicit escalation signal rather than a timeout.

Implemented per-call session isolation. A fresh session per pipeline invocation keeps raw search results, internal drafts, and critique logs out of the user's conversation context, a production concern absent from typical multi-agent demos.

Deployed a deterministic code-based keyword filter ahead of all tool access, making the security guardrail structurally bypass-resistant, with a deliberate worker/critic model split for quality-cost balance.

title: Crypto Accumulation Scanner
layer1: Derived an original volatility baseline by log-log regression on 2020 to 2024 market data, ln(Vol%) ≈ 1.2 × ln(MarketCap) − 24.8.
bullets: Derived an original volatility baseline by log-log regression on 2020 to 2024 market data, ln(Vol%) ≈ 1.2 × ln(MarketCap) − 24.8, normalising each asset against its market-cap tier so genuine outliers surface instead of size artefacts.

Solved platform constraints: chunked storage across a 500KB per-key limit, execution-timeout safety with progress persistence and auto-resume, exchange symbol-prefix normalisation (1000SHIB to SHIB with price scaled), and time-weighted volatility correcting for partial-candle distortion.

layer1: 85%+ solve rate within six guesses across a 5,922-word list, covered by a 36-test suite.
